label: A serious relationship you ended for this
blurb: You were going to marry her. You told her the truth, and she took it better than you deserved.
outcome: You know what you are giving up, which is more than most of the men can say. You will be good with couples and terrible on certain anniversaries. She may write. She may not.

risk.label: The woman he was going to marry

label: A bad period with drink, ended
blurb: Two years, maybe three, that you do not fully remember. Sober now, and you know exactly how long.
outcome: You know what it is to be forgiven and to be watched. The recovery people in every parish will find you within a month. A rectory with a full liquor cabinet and a lonely pastor is a place you will have to be careful in for the rest of your life.

label: Money trouble, or a bankruptcy
blurb: A business that failed, a loan that went wrong, a number you still remember.
outcome: You have read a balance sheet with your own name on it, which is a better education than any course. You will never be casual about a parish's money. The number is still out there, in a database, and someone may find it.

label: A political past, with an arrest
blurb: A cause, a march, a night in a holding cell that your mother still does not know about.
outcome: You have said things in public and you know what it costs. You already have the habit of the loud, consistent position, which is either the making of you or the end of you depending on who the bishop is. The photograph exists.

label: A breakdown, and a hospital
blurb: Some weeks in college when it all came apart, and a ward where you learned to put it back.
outcome: You know the inside of a psychiatric unit, which makes you the priest the desperate can talk to. You also know that the formation faculty have your file, and that a diocese under pressure can read a file however it likes.

label: A child you support and rarely see
blurb: Before any of this. The mother married someone else. You send money, and a card on birthdays, and you have told the vocation director.
outcome: The diocese knows, and has decided it can live with it, for now. You will be a better father to other people's children than most of the presbyterate, and you will pay for it every birthday. If it becomes public at the wrong moment, it will be read as a scandal whatever the truth is.
